claims.text: US President Donald Trump's approval rating dropped to 33 percent, matching the lowest point of his presidency, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.
According to the American Automobile Association, US gasoline prices rose by nearly a third compared to a year prior.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 80 percent of Americans believe US involvement in Iran will continue for an extended period.
US President Donald Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it interferes with US negotiations with Iran, according to Fox News.
Approximately one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas passes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated that Iran and Oman reached an understanding on transit route maps through the Strait of Hormuz.
An Iranian news agency Tasnim spokesperson denied Donald Trump's claim that the US maintains a direct backchannel with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Hotel occupancy in Dubai fell from 80 percent to around 10 percent after Iran launched strikes against US allies in response to US-Israel attacks.
The United Arab Emirates introduced a $680 million package to support businesses affected by the Iran war.
Two Hadid-110 drones launched from Iranian territory targeted Kurdistan Regional Government Prime Minister Masrour Barzani's office and a regional security chief's residence.
US Ambassador to Iraq Tom Barrack condemned the drone strikes in Iraqi Kurdistan as a direct threat to regional stability.
Donald Trump stated in the Oval Office that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un responded positively to his diplomatic overtures.
US envoy Jared Kushner stated that progress toward Gaza demilitarization could materialize in as little as 30 days.
Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that the US would substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea.
Donald Trump explicitly linked scaling back joint drills to South Korea's refusal to assist in US operations regarding Iran.
Approximately 28,500 American military personnel are stationed in South Korea.
South Korea's presidential Blue House stated it would review Donald Trump's comments while continuing diplomatic consultations.
Joint military drills between South Korea and the US proceeded on Monday despite Donald Trump's order to scale them back.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US envoy Jared Kushner agreed that an American general will oversee the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza.
Israeli military forces currently control approximately 60 percent of the Gaza Strip.
Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Jordan, Pakistan, and Indonesia issued a joint statement condemning Israel's rejection of the US-backed ceasefire proposal.
Jared Kushner left Jerusalem without a breakthrough after holding two days of talks with Israeli and Hamas leaders.
Benjamin Netanyahu and Jared Kushner agreed to establish working groups focused on Gaza's demilitarization and public health.
Far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir stated in a podcast interview that Israel should kill 30 to 40 people every night in Gaza.
Gaza's health ministry reported at least 1,265 Palestinians killed by Israeli military operations since the ceasefire went into effect on October 10.
Jared Kushner met with Hamas political chief Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt prior to travelling to Jerusalem.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu was heckled during a visit to Le Porge, where 183 homes were destroyed by wildfires.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced €12 million in government aid for the fire-affected Gironde and Landes regions.
Two people died and hundreds were evacuated due to twin wildfires on the Greek island of Salamina.
A Spanish soldier died while battling the Peñas de Riglos wildfire in the Aragón region of Spain.
Britain deployed military personnel to assist as wildfires spread across European nations.
France sent 104 firefighters and 36 emergency vehicles to assist Spanish authorities battling wildfires in Aragón.
The EU's Copernicus service confirmed western Europe experienced its warmest June-to-July period on record.
Germany, Sweden, Norway, and the Netherlands dispatched emergency aerial and ground reinforcements to support Belgium's wildfire response.
Data from the European Forest Fire Information System showed 576,000 hectares of land burned across Europe in 2026.
Approximately 30 residents in the German border town of Monschau received evacuation orders as High Fens wildfires approached.
The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak killed 2,325 people, making it the country's deadliest Ebola epidemic on record.
The DRC Public Health Institute reported total confirmed Ebola cases reached 4,945, with 101 new cases detected in 24 hours.
More than 3,400 confirmed Ebola cases were recorded in DRC's Ituri province.
Uganda declared itself Ebola-free on July 28 after discharging its final treated patient.
WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated that two vaccines developed specifically for the Bundibugyo strain are undergoing clinical trials.
The UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency granted approval for human trials of a Oxford University-developed Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine.
A 7.7-magnitude earthquake in eastern Indonesia killed at least 68 people and injured over 200 others.
East Nusa Tenggara province registered nearly 1,600 aftershocks following the magnitude 7.7 earthquake.
Maria Florida Nogo Kelen underwent emergency C-section surgery to give birth during the earthquake in eastern Indonesia.
Dr. Melinda, the sole physician at the Dampek Health Centre on Flores island, issued an urgent plea for help while treating hundreds of quake victims.
The 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck Flores island at a depth of 15 kilometers shortly before 06:00 local time on Saturday.
The earthquake in eastern Indonesia damaged more than 900 buildings and displaced nearly 13,000 people.
Deepak Mhaskey was appointed as the BJP's new national social media convener, replacing long-serving predecessor Amit Malviya.
Deepak Mhaskey previously worked as a college chemistry professor and served as head of the BJP social media cell in Chhattisgarh.
Former Union minister Smriti Irani was appointed BJP national general secretary in charge of Uttar Pradesh.
The BJP's vote share in Uttar Pradesh fell from around 50 percent in 2019 to approximately 41 percent in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.
The BJP's newly announced national leadership team under President Nitin Nabin includes 12 women leaders.
Former Aligarh Muslim University vice chancellor Professor Tariq Mansoor was appointed BJP national vice president.
Smriti Irani, Biplab Deb, Sunil Bansal, Vinod Tawde, Gajendra Patel, Satish Poonia, Harish Dwivedi, and Sanjay Bhatia were named BJP national general secretaries.
Nearly 50 of the 65 office-bearers named in the BJP's national team reshuffle are new appointments.
Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto ended his hunger strike after Chief Minister Hemant Soren agreed to cancel disputed recruitment exams.
Protesting Jharkhand students organized under the JPSC-JSSC Abhyarthi Nyay Manch and JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch platforms in Ranchi.
Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination and all activities associated with agency TDPL.
The Jharkhand government ordered a comprehensive CID investigation into recruitment exam errors occurring since 2014.
The Jharkhand government decided to form an examination reforms committee headed by senior IAS officer Amitabh Kaushal.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi sent a letter to Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren urging him to meet directly with protesting students.
Demonstrating students in Ranchi held sit-in protests at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, with six going on an indefinite hunger strike.
